equity_bridge.item: Long-term investments (available-for-sale debt and marketable equity securities)
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 10-K balance sheet; their income is in 'interest income and other', outside the flows

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle revenue growth after the China deconsolidation (comps 2-3% plus low-single-digit unit growth, increasingly licensed). Equity CAGR is unusable: shareholders' equity has been negative since FY2019.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Shareholders' deficit of -7,669 (buybacks and dividends ahead of retained earnings) makes the house-default equity CAGR meaningless. EPS CAGRs are negative because FY2026 GAAP EPS of 2.21 carries 688.6 of restructuring and a 34.2% effective tax rate; non-GAAP EPS was 2.72.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC and equity-award withholding taxes): FY2021 4,103.0, FY2022 2,157.2, FY2023 3,283.1, FY2024 2,909.4, FY2025 2,036.3, FY2026 3,283.2. Owner FCF has gone nowhere for five years, and FY2026's recovery came from a 1.0bn capex cut rather than from operations.

scenario_narratives.base: Back to Starbucks works but normalises. North America comps slow from 6.6% in FY2026 to the guided ~4% in FY2027 and 3% thereafter; company-operated openings resume from FY2028 once development capability is rebuilt, and international growth is licensed and capital-light, led by the China JV. Reported revenue dips 1% in FY2027 on the China deconsolidation and steps back in FY2028 as the 53rd week is lapped. The operating margin climbs from the guided 13.5-14.0% back to 17% over nine years, the level the business earned in FY2021 and FY2023, as restructuring ends and labour investment is leveraged. Capex returns to about 5% of revenue from FY2026's depressed 3.3%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Niccol repeats the Chipotle playbook: transaction growth holds at 3-4% for several years on Green Apron Service, the tiered Rewards programme and faster throughput, so North America comps run 4-5% and unit growth returns to 3-4%. The China JV scales toward its 20,000-store aspiration and pays rising royalties and equity income for no capital. Margins pass the old peak and reach 19%, because a quarter of the system that used to be company-operated in China is now royalty revenue.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY2026 comp surge was bought with labour hours and lapped easy comparisons after two years of negative traffic. Once lapped, US traffic goes flat against Dutch Bros, Dunkin' and McDonald's, a consumer slowdown hits a premium discretionary ticket, and a first Workers United contract plus elevated arabica prices keep the added cost in place. Margins stall at 13-13.5%, below guidance, more closures follow, and China contributes little as Luckin-style price competition caps the JV's earnings. No solvency question arises: the 13.3bn of debt is serviceable in every year of this path.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Starbucks is valued on unlevered owner free cash flow built from guided operating margins, not on FY2026's reported FCF, which was lifted by a one-year capex cut and low cash taxes. The market price capitalises FY2027 guided non-GAAP EPS at roughly 33x; this model lets margins recover all the way to the prior 16-17% peak and still does not get there, because owner FCF has been flat for five years and the recovery in it has yet to come from operations. The gap to the price is mostly a discount-rate and duration disagreement: the price sits above the base-case value even at a 6.5% required return, where the terminal value is already held at the 20x cap.
key_risks_to_valuation: FY2027 revenue guidance is taken second-hand from the earnings release; if underlying revenue is nearer the H2 FY2026 run-rate, every scenario is a few percent too low
Maintenance capex after the China exit is unproven: each 1pp of revenue in capex is worth roughly 6 per share in the base case
The margin path is the whole valuation: 17% versus 13.5% terminal operating margin is the difference between base and bear
Income from equity investees (China JV, North American Coffee Partnership) is inside the flows at book income, while cash distributions ran 110 below it in FY2026
The Nestle prepaid royalty adjustment (0.45pp of margin) is inferred from the movement in long-term deferred revenue, not from a disclosed amortisation figure

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 81.97-111.50
data_sources.financials: SBUX_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL) and SBUX_Annual_FY2026.txt: statements of earnings, balance sheet, cash flows, EPS note, equity method investments note, liquidity section
data_sources.qualitative: SBUX_Analysis.json (2026-11-15), including FY2027 guidance from the Q4 FY2026 earnings release of 2026-10-29

inputs.share_count_basis: 1,140.1m shares outstanding at 5 Nov 2026 (FY2026 10-K cover) plus 4.1m dilutive options/RSUs (FY2026 EPS note, treasury-stock method). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; resumed FY2027 buybacks are the cash mechanism for that and are value-neutral here.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement: stock-based compensation 368.6 plus minimum tax withholdings on share-based awards 73.0 (financing). Starbucks publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: Sunday closest to 30 September (FY2026 ended 27 Sep 2026; FY2027 is a 53-week year)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST) + beta ~0.95 x 5.0% ERP = cost of equity ~9.0%; debt ~10% of capital (13.3bn against ~122bn market cap) at ~4.5% pre-tax, ~3.4% after tax. WACC ~8.5%. One rate for all three scenarios: risk is carried by the scenario weights, not by a per-scenario discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: rent is an operating expense inside EBITDA (cash paid on operating leases 1,943.9 in FY2026), so the 9,136.7 of operating lease liabilities is NOT in net debt and lease_cost_pct_path is zero. One treatment, not two.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests 7.3 on the balance sheet and -0.6 of earnings: immaterial, ignored.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (mature operating company, positive FCF; routed via dcf-methods, first valuation of this ticker). Net debt = current + long-term debt 13,276.9 less cash 3,679.9 and short-term investments 184.3; long-term investments 309.5 go through the equity bridge. No interest income is stripped: the company is in net debt, and interest income sits below operating income so it was never in the EBITDA path. EBITDA path is built from the non-GAAP operating margin (FY2026 11.9%, FY2027 guided 13.5-14.0%) plus D&A plus the SBC expense added back (0.98% of revenue; the engine then deducts 1.15% including equity-award withholding taxes), LESS 0.45pp for the non-cash amortisation of the Nestle Global Coffee Alliance prepaid royalty (long-term deferred revenue fell 190.0 in FY2026; that revenue was collected and taxed in FY2018-FY2020 and brings no cash). Income from equity investees (294.8 in FY2026, including the 40% China JV from Q3) is left inside operating income and therefore inside the flows, so the 1,784.1 of equity investments is deliberately NOT added to the bridge; cash distributions (187.9) ran below booked income in FY2026, which roughly offsets the engine taxing an already after-tax line. FY2026 reported FCF of 3,724.8 is flattered: capex fell to 1,263.6 (3.3% of revenue, against 6.2-7.7% in FY2024-FY2025) and cash taxes of 684.0 ran well below the 1,315.0 provision; management expects FY2027 capex to be higher. The forward build uses ~5% capex and a 25% cash tax rate rather than carrying the FY2026 margin. FY2027 revenue guidance (about -1% including roughly 700 from the 53rd week) is taken from the Q4 FY2026 release as recorded in the Analysis JSON; the 10-K itself only says 'moderation in net revenues'. That guide looks low against the H2 FY2026 post-China run-rate (about 18.5bn for the half) and deserves a check against Q1 FY2027. Buybacks: none in FY2025 or FY2026; a resumption is planned for FY2027 with 29.8m shares authorised, no dollar amount given.

bear.margin_rationale: Non-GAAP operating margin misses FY2027 guidance at 13.0% and settles at 13.5%: the labour hours that bought the comp recovery stay in the cost base.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 is FY2027 guidance (about -1% including the 53rd week). Year 2 laps that week (about -1.9pp) on ~5% underlying growth. Then North America comps of 3-4% plus resumed unit growth, fading to 3%.
base.margin_rationale: Non-GAAP operating margin 13.75% (guidance midpoint) rising to 17.0% by year 9: back to the FY2021/FY2023 peak of 16-17%, helped by the licensed China mix. EBITDA = operating margin + D&A + 0.53 (SBC expense added back, Nestle non-cash royalty removed).

bull.margin_rationale: Non-GAAP operating margin reaches 19% by year 9, two points above any year in the company's history, on sales leverage and a structurally more licensed mix.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% rather than the 15% default: the turnaround has four quarters of evidence, not a cycle's worth, 76% of revenue rides on one mature market, and guidance already has comps decelerating. Base 50%: it is management's own FY2027 guide extended back to margins the company has earned before. Bull 30% rather than 35%: it needs sustained traffic growth and a margin the company has never reported, two things that have to go right together.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
